title: The Funny story about the dog
subtitle: 戏剧表演 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 戏剧表演（文学艺术与体育·戏剧与表演）
meta: 主题语境：戏剧表演（文学艺术与体育·戏剧与表演）　|　核心词汇：funny　|　正文 336 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 funny 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1948 the elder wrote of ① a funny story about the dog in the memoir, and everybody in the village said at once that it was ② funnier than the one named there the year before. Three years on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the elder, who never explained anything, had done it before dawn and gone home; it was the funny ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the funniest story about the dog anybody in the village had ever seen, or so the memoir for November 1942 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too funny to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the youth who had come to help; the funny ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the staff at the far gate, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a funny noise in the roof, and said that no youth in his right mind would call it ⑥ as funny as the noise in the roof they had once had in the old village. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was funny or not, and he said so.

By 1955 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the memoir. What the line asked for was ⑦ something funny, and nothing besides. The youth from the next village called the whole plan ⑧ quite funny; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the memoir kept the names of the funny ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1958, in public, she wrote of another funny story about the dog in the same memoir, and the work, which took two years, seemed ⑨ funnier than anybody had expected. ⑩ The funniest noise in the roof in the whole village, she said in 1960, was the one she could never quite name; the funny ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 滑稽（前置定语 a funny story about the dog：1948 年长者在回忆录里记下的那件滑稽的趣事）
B. adj. 滑稽／古怪（比较级 funnier than：文中两处，一处比关于那条狗的趣事，一处比预想）
C. adj. 滑稽／古怪（最高级 the funniest：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 滑稽（表语 too funny to do：母亲觉得它太滑稽，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 古怪（前置定语 a funny noise in the roof：叔叔把整件事称作一桩古怪的怪响）
F. adj. 古怪（同级比较 as funny as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩屋顶上的怪响相比）
G. adj. 古怪（后置定语 something funny：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 古怪（受程度副词修饰 quite funny：那位后生的评价）

items.q: a funny story about the dog
the funniest story about the dog anybody
a funny noise in the roof
The funniest noise in the roof in

answers.why: funny 意为“滑稽”，1948 年长者在回忆录里记下的是“一件滑稽的趣事”，此处作前置定语 a funny story about the dog。
funny 意为“滑稽”，此处用比较级 funnier than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
funny 意为“滑稽”，回忆录上 十一月 那行字说它是村子里最滑稽的一件，故用最高级 the funniest story about the dog。
funny 意为“滑稽”，母亲认为这件东西“太滑稽了，谁也用不上”，too funny to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
funny 意为“古怪”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩古怪的怪响”，此处作前置定语 a funny noise in the roof。
funny 意为“古怪”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩屋顶上的怪响一样古怪”，同级比较用 as funny as。
funny 意为“古怪”，回忆录上那半行字要的是“古怪的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something funny。
funny 意为“古怪”，邻村子来的那位后生认为这套计划“相当古怪”，quite 修饰原级 funny。
funny 意为“古怪”，1958 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要古怪”，故用比较级 funnier than。
funny 意为“古怪”，母亲 1960 年说的是“整个村子里最古怪的那一桩”，故用最高级 the funniest noise in the roof。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1948 年，长者在回忆录里记下了一件滑稽的趣事。（a funny story about the dog）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更滑稽。（funnier than …）
母亲觉得它太滑稽，谁也用不上。（too funny to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩古怪的怪响。（a funny noise in the roof）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩屋顶上的怪响一样古怪。（as funny as …）
到了 1955 年，回忆录上只剩半行字：要的是一件古怪的东西。（something funny）
answers: In 1948 the elder wrote of a funny story about the dog in the memoir.
Everybody said it was funnier than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too funny to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a funny noise in the roof.
He said nobody would call it as funny as the noise in the roof they had once had.
By 1955 the memoir asked for nothing but something funny.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 funny 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1948 the elder wrote of a funny story about the dog in the memoir, and nobody forgot it.
It was the funniest story about the dog in the village, or so the memoir says.
My mother thought it too funny to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a funny noise in the roof, and nobody argued with him.
The youth from the next village called the plan quite funny, and everybody laughed.
The funny ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
